_meta.convention: Every block has verified true/false. verified=true means read in the cited primary document (or official result page) during this research. Article numbers refer to the cited issue.

regulations.technical: FIA 2026 F1 Regulations Section C Issue 17 (28 Apr 2026)

sessions.name: FP2
sessions.rule: 2-3 h after FP1; 90 min if ICTT tyre testing scheduled

sessions.name: Race
sessions.maxDuration: 2 h running, 3 h total incl. suspensions

sessions.name: Sprint Qualifying
sessions.rule: 2.5-3.5 h after FP1; SQ1/SQ2 new Medium only, SQ3 Soft only

sprint.parcFerme: Parc fermé from first exit in SQ until Sprint start; again from first exit in Qualifying until Race start.

qualifying.rule107: Q1 eliminees slower than 107% of fastest Q1 time are unclassified (unless wet); stewards decide start.
qualifying.note: Pre-season articles stated Q3 12 min; Issue 07 text has 13 min (break shortened by 1 min).

parcFerme.from: car's first exit from pit lane in Qualifying (Sprint Qualifying at sprint events)
parcFerme.rule: No parts replaced/modified and no set-up/configuration change except Appendix B2 permitted work or with Technical Delegate approval; suspension set-up sheet submitted before first run. Breach = start from pit lane.
parcFerme.exception: 6 times per season, damaged front wing/rear wing/rear bodywork/floor may be replaced by a different previously-raced specification (B3.5.5).

mass.minimumMass: 724 kg + Nominal Tyre Mass (all sessions except qualifying); 726 kg + Nominal Tyre Mass in Qualifying and Sprint Qualifying
mass.headlineFigure: 768 kg is the commonly quoted total (722/724 kg + ~46 kg nominal tyre set mass); the regulation defines it as 724 kg + Nominal Tyre Mass (Pirelli-measured set mass, rounded to 1 kg).
mass.excludes: fuel (Car Mass = car incl. tyres + driver + driver ballast)
mass.weightDistribution: front axle >= 0.44 x minimum mass, rear axle >= 0.54 x minimum mass (qualifying)
mass.driverMass: Reference mass of driver (measured in race kit per FIA-F1-DOC-035) + driver ballast must be >= 82 kg at all times (C4.5.2). NOTE: it is driver (+ballast), not 'driver + seat'.
mass.driverBallast: Fixed between front and rear of cockpit entry template, attached to survival cell, sealed, density > 7500 kg/m3 (C4.3.2)
mass.heatHazard: +5 kg in race/sprint (TTCS), +2 kg in practice/qualifying when Heat Hazard declared (cooling vest)

fuel.refuelling: Not permitted during Race/Sprint (C4.4: no substance may be added during Race or Sprint); refuelling only in garage outside sessions at <= 0.8 l/s
fuel.fuelEnergyFlow: max 3000 MJ/h; below 10,500 rpm max EF = 0.27*rpm + 165 MJ/h; partial-load curve EF = 9.78*P_engine(kW) + 869 MJ/h (380 MJ/h at <= -50 kW)
fuel.raceFuelLimit: No explicit race fuel mass/energy cap found in Issue 17 Section C or Issue 07 Section B; limitation is via energy flow. Media estimates ~70 kg race fuel load (unverified).
fuel.verifyNote: Flow limits verified (C5.2.3-C5.2.5); 'no race fuel mass limit' is absence-of-finding; ~70 kg figure unverified.

ers.mguK: 350 kW max electrical DC power; MGU-H removed; MGU-K torque max 500 Nm; MGU-K usable at standing start only from 50 km/h
ers.deploymentNormal: P(kW) <= 1800 - 5*v(km/h) for v<340; 6900-20*v for 340<=v<345; 0 at >=345 km/h (capped at 350 kW, i.e. full 350 kW up to 290 km/h)
ers.deploymentOvertake: P(kW) <= 7100 - 20*v for v<355 (capped 350 kW, i.e. full power to 337.5 km/h); 0 at >=355 km/h
ers.raceSectorLimit: On FIA-specified sectors in Race/Sprint: 250 kW below 310 km/h then normal taper (C5.2.8.iii, added for safety)
ers.recharge: max 8.5 MJ per lap (may be reduced per circuit; qualifying limit reduced to no less than 5 MJ at up to 12 events; reported reduction 8 -> 7 MJ for qualifying from Miami); +0.5 MJ extra harvest per lap when Overtake is activated
ers.boost: Driver-activated mode that maintains/increases ERS-K power demand

overtakeMode.race: Activated at the Activation Line if car was within the Detection Gap of a car ahead at the Detection Line (FIA sets gap per event; widely reported as 1.0 s - unverified); disabled first lap after start/restart until leader crosses Detection Line; disabled under SC until cars cross Line after SC enters pits; disabled in Low Grip conditions

ers.midSeasonChange: From Miami: 'super clipping' limit raised 250 -> 350 kW to cut lift-and-coast; qualifying harvest 8 -> 7 MJ (Wikipedia, citing FIA)
ers.verifyNote: Formulas verified in C5.2; detection-gap value and Miami change details from secondary sources (verified=false for those).

modes.cornerMode: high-downforce default; failure returns wings to Corner Mode
modes.straightMode: front-wing flaps and rear-wing flap to low-drag position ('X-mode'/'straight-line mode')

activeAero.use: Driver may fully activate (front+rear) in FIA-defined Activation Zones when enabled; Low Grip conditions: partial activation only (front wing only) in Low Grip Activation Zones. Available to all drivers every lap (not proximity-based).

tyres.raceRule: In a dry race each driver must use >= 2 different dry specifications, at least one being a mandatory race specification (DSQ if not). Not required if inters/wets used.
tyres.q3Rule: One set of the softest spec reserved for Q3
tyres.returns: Standard weekend: 2 sets returned after FP1, 2 after FP2, 2 after FP3
tyres.blankets: Allowed: resistive blankets acting on outer surface, max 3 controllable zones (C10.8.4); blankets on fitted wheels must be disconnected from power on the grid (B5). Max blanket temperature is set by Pirelli prescriptions (70 C for all slicks in 2025) - 2026 value not verified.
tyres.verifyNote: Allocation/race-rule verified in B6; blanket temperature verified=false.

pitLaneSpeed.note: Race Director may amend (historically 60 km/h at Monaco/Singapore/Baku etc.; per-event values not verified)

safetyCar.vsc: All cars reduce speed and stay above an FIA-ECU minimum (delta) time; no overtaking; pitting allowed
safetyCar.sc: Field bunches behind SC; Overtake mode disabled until all cars cross the Line after SC pits

bop.note: No BoP in F1; ADUO (additional development and upgrade opportunities) for PU manufacturers that fall behind exists in 2026 regs (not detailed here, unverified)

pitStops.tyreChange: no crew-size limit specified in regs (typically ~20 mechanics, unverified)

wec.regulations: 2026 FIA WEC Sporting Regulations v1.2 (WMSC 16 Oct 2025, applies from 1 Jan 2026); Le Mans 2026 Supplementary Regulations

sessions.name: Free practice
sessions.rule: 2 or 3 sessions of 1 h / 1.5 h / 2 h, total max 4 h; typical FP1 90 min, FP2 90 min, FP3 60 min

sessions.name: LMGT3 Qualifying
sessions.rule: Bronze driver only; sets grid P11+

sessions.name: LMGT3 Hyperpole
sessions.rule: top 10 from qualifying; Silver driver only (if crew has one) - sets P1-10

sixHour.typicalTimes: Practice Thu/Fri, qualifying block late Fri/Sat afternoon (~16:00-17:30 local), race Sat/Sun midday (11:00-14:00 local)

eightTenHour.note: 8 h (Bahrain, cancelled 2026) / 10 h or 1812 km (Qatar, cancelled 2026) use same quali format with larger tyre allocation and 8-10 h points scale

sessions.name: Free Practice 1-4
sessions.detail: 1 x 1 h, 1 x 2 h, 2 x 3 h (incl. night sessions)

sessions.name: Qualifying (Q)
sessions.detail: Hypercar session >=30 min; LMP2+LMGT3 session >=30 min

sessions.name: Hyperpole 1 (H1)
sessions.detail: Hypercar top 15 from Q, >=20 min, sets P11-15; LMP2/LMGT3 top 12 (marked-up text changed 15->12) sets P9-12
sessions.verifyNote: LMGT3/LMP2 numbers read from a marked-up document with strikethroughs; Hypercar numbers clear

sessions.name: Hyperpole 2 (H2)
sessions.detail: Hypercar top 10 from H1, >=15 min, sets P1-10; LMP2/LMGT3 top 8 (changed from 10)

points.pole: +1 point to car with best Hyperpole time in each category (crew + team; manufacturers via that car)
points.hypercarManufacturers: Two cars designated per manufacturer score per the race scale
points.hypercarDrivers: World Championship; crews scoring same points share
points.lmgt3: FIA Endurance Trophy for drivers and teams (per car number)
points.minimumDriving: Driver with < 45 min total driving scores no points
points.shortenedRace: <2 green laps: no points; >2 laps but <75% of race time: half points; >75%: full

driverTimes.hypercar: no class-specific min/max table; 45 min to score points

crewComposition.lmgt3: 2-3 drivers incl. >=1 Bronze plus another Bronze or a Silver

parcFerme.rule: Cars not eligible for Hyperpole go into parc fermé at end of qualifying; Hyperpole cars at end of Hyperpole. Refuelling forbidden during quali/Hyperpole sessions; work incl. refuelling and tyre change allowed on Hyperpole cars between qualifying and Hyperpole. Set-up otherwise free between practice and race (no general F1-style parc fermé).
parcFerme.verifyNote: the 'set-up otherwise free' statement is an inference, not explicitly read

mass.hyper: Minimum mass per BoP table (BoP tables no longer published from 2026). LMH/LMDh base minimum ~1030 kg (unverified for 2026).

driverCompensation.hyper: Reference crew weight 82 kg for Qualifying/Hyperpole (vs lightest driver taking part) and 78 kg for the race (vs average declared crew weight); ballast = ref - average, rounded up, max -5 kg; plus qualifying BSFC compensation ballast per manufacturer
driverCompensation.lmgt3: Reference crew weight 82 kg all sessions; ballast in homologated ballast box; max -5 kg
driverCompensation.weightIncludes: driver with full safety kit incl. helmet/HANS and personal seat insert

mass.verifyNote: compensation ballast verified (WEC_2026_D06 amended 02/07/2026); Hypercar base mass unverified

energyAndFuel.hyperVirtualEnergyTank: Max deployed energy per stint (PPUEnergyStint, per-car BoP value, measured by driveshaft torque sensors, pit-out to pit-in). PPUEnergyTank refills while refuel hose connected at PPUEnergyFlow = PPUEnergyStint/40 s (i.e. full refill ~40 s) after a BoP-defined 'additional docking time'. Overdraw = penalty and deficit made up at next stop.
energyAndFuel.lmgt3: Also subject to a per-stint energy/fuel limit via BoP (virtual energy tank concept since 2024) - not read in a 2026 document
energyAndFuel.refuelling: Allowed, only in the stopping area at start of stop, engine off; 1 refueller + deadman-valve attendant + extinguisher attendant; during refuelling max 4 persons may only ground the car, clean, visually check tyres/brakes - no tools, so tyres are changed after refuelling
energyAndFuel.pitCrew: Max 4 persons (armbands) to work on car; max 2 pneumatic wheel guns; 2 industry reps may check tyres/brakes; driver change allowed anytime during stop
energyAndFuel.fcyEmergencyStop: Under FCY/SC closed pit: emergency stop allowed (8 s refuel + docking time, damaged tyres) once per FCY

specsPerSeason.hyper: 3 dry specs at Le Mans, 2 at other races (3 total over season) + 1 wet
specsPerSeason.lmgt3: 2 dry specs (2 at all races) + 1 wet

tyres.wets: Unlimited, only when track declared wet
tyres.hypercarRandomSets: Technical Delegates may randomly assign one set of each spec (29/34 tyre layout)
tyres.blankets: Tyre warmers forbidden in WEC (long-standing rule; not re-read in 2026 doc)

neutralisations.fcy: 80 km/h, single file, no overtaking; pit entry closed (emergency stop only), exit open
neutralisations.vsc: 80 km/h, used ~2 laps before SC is deployed; each VSC followed by SC
neutralisations.sc: Multiple safety cars (Le Mans 3); pit entry rules per SC procedure
neutralisations.slowZone: Le Mans uses Slow Zones (80 km/h) - not re-read in 2026 doc (verified=false)

bop.mechanism: FIA/ACO set per-car BoP (min weight, max power vs speed, energy per stint, docking time) per event; Hypercar also BSFC quali ballast. From 2026 BoP tables are no longer published.
bop.lmgt3: BoP per model (weight, power, energy per stint); no success ballast in WEC

gt4.regulationsNote: 2026 Sporting Regulations not publicly retrievable; rules below from the 2024 GT4ES Sporting Regulations (S02) unless confirmed by a 2026 stewards' bulletin. verified=false where only 2024 text was available.

weekendFormat.rule: Q1 driver starts Race 1, Q2 driver starts Race 2 (order may be reversed by event regs)
weekendFormat.verifyNote: 2024 regs Art. 41.7; 2026 confirmed two 60-min races with mandatory stop

pitStop.mandatory: One stop per race with driver change; pit window opens 25:00 and closes 34:59.99 after start (delayed if SC/FCY)

minimumTime2026.monza: 80 s (driver change only); 150 s if tyres changed during mandatory stop or outside window

pitStop.minimumTimeFormula: pit-lane delta at 50 km/h + 50 s (2024 regs); +1 s tolerance once per event
pitStop.tyreChange: Only for weather change (all 4) or confirmed damage
pitStop.soloDriver: If permitted to race alone, must exit and re-enter car during the stop
pitStop.successPenalty: No results-based success time penalty found; driver-categorisation derogations may add pit-stop time
pitStop.verifyNote: 2026 times verified from Monza/Portimão bulletins; window/formula from 2024 regs (verified=false)

points.qualifyingPole: +1 point for fastest in each of Q1 and Q2 per category (Silver, Pro-Am, Am)
points.teams: Only highest-finishing car per team per category scores

mass.car: Per SRO GT4 BoP sheet per model and event
mass.driverWeight: Average driver weight per car must be >= 85 kg; otherwise driver ballast to compensate (2024 regs 28.7)

fuel.refuelling: Not allowed during any session or race (paddock only); fuel TotalEnergies; >= 2 kg fuel for sampling
fuel.verifyNote: 2024 regs Art. 35; consistent with TotalEnergies fuel reps in 2026 bulletins

tyres.wet: Cinturato WHB (reported for GTWC Europe 2026; GT4-specific wet not stated)
tyres.allocation: 1st event: 4 new sets (S1-S2 FP/pre-quali; S3-S4 quali and races). Later events: 3 new sets + 1 used set from previous event (S1, FP only). 1 joker tyre per event. Wets unlimited (when declared wet in FP/quali; free choice in races).
tyres.verifyNote: allocation from 2024 regs; DHG from Tyrepress 2026 GTWC article

neutralisations.sc: Safety Car; pit window delayed/extended if SC/FCY at window open

bop.mechanism: SRO GT Bureau BoP (weight, restrictor/power, ride height etc.) issued per event: e.g. 'BALANCE OF PERFORMANCE FOR PORTIMAO', SRO GT Bureau 09/10/2026

sessions.name: Qualifying
sessions.detail: Q1 20 min all cars; >=5 min break; Q2 10 min top 12

sessions.name: Race 1
sessions.duration: min 25 min + 1 lap (exact time-based length per event Appendix 1)

weekendFormat.race2Grid: Top 10 of qualifying reversed (P10 on pole), P11-12 from Q2, rest by Q1
weekendFormat.pitStops: No mandatory pit stop; no refuelling during sessions

points.teams: Two nominated drivers per team score

mass.minimumRacingWeight: Car min weight (TCR Tech Regs 2.5) + driver in full kit + BoP ballast; sprint car with racing gearbox 1265 kg incl. driver (1230 kg with production gearbox); max 1415 kg incl. fuel, driver, ballast
mass.driverWeighing: Drivers weighed in full kit at first event and mid-season; weight included in min racing weight (no fixed reference driver weight)
mass.verifyNote: 1265/1230 kg read in 2026 TCR Tech Regs; the exact article context (BoP reference vs absolute) not fully parsed

successBallast.name: Compensation Weight (CW)
successBallast.basis: Drivers' total points collected at the current event (qualifying + both races); applied for the whole next event on top of car+driver weight, even above min racing weight
successBallast.overMaxWeight: Excess beyond max car weight converted to +5 mm (<=10 kg) or +10 mm (>10 kg) ride height
successBallast.raceByRaceEntry: +20 kg at first appearance in last two rounds

bop.mechanism: WSC TCR BoP per model (min racing weight, power, ride height etc.) via Technical Bulletins + CW

fuel.refuelling: Forbidden during practice, qualifying and races; single designated fuel supplier

tyres.dry: Kumho Ecsta S700 slick (TCR-wide Kumho spec; verified=false for TCR Europe)
tyres.allocation: 1st event max 12 new dry tyres; from 2nd event max 14 dry tyres of which max 8 new (+2 new at Paul Ricard and Monza); max 12 wet tyres per event
tyres.blankets: Tyre warmers and any heat-retention devices forbidden

neutralisations.fcy: 60 km/h single file, no overtaking; pit entry and exit open
